title: Prompt-to-CICD SDK adopter tutorial outline (draft)
content:
Goal: A compact, hands-on tutorial that takes a software engineer from prompt experimentation to production-safe CI/CD for Redwood SDK usage. Focus: repeatable labs, telemetry contracts, simple gating, and rollback patterns — minimal theory, maximal runbook-ready steps. Audience: - Product/Platform engineers who will integrate Redwood SDK into services - Solutions engineers helping customers adopt prompt-based features - New developer hires on the Developer Experience team Outcomes (what learners can do after the tutorial): 1) Produce a small prompt-driven endpoint locally using the Redwood SDK and a sample model. 2) Write unit + integration tests that mock model outputs and assert quality thresholds. 3) Add CI steps that run prompt-evals and raise a failure on quality regression. 4) Implement minimal telemetry and an automated canary rollout with fast rollback. Mini-curriculum (4 x 60–90 minute modules): Module A — Local prompt lab (setup + iterate) - Objective: fast feedback loop for prompt tuning. - Steps: clone sample, virtualenv, ri sdk init, export REDWOOD_API_KEY, run sample_app.py. - Exercise: given customer-support prompt template, iterate to reduce hallucinations in 3 tries. - Deliverable: repo branch with final prompt and a short note on failure modes. Module B — Unit and integration tests for prompts - Objective: make prompts testable and deterministic in CI. - Pattern: dependency-inject a model-client interface; provide a mock responder for unit tests. - Example test (pytest-like): def test_summarize_handles_html(): mock_client = MockModelClient(responses=["clean summary"]) svc = Summarizer(client=mock_client) assert "clean" in svc.summarize("

long content

") - Integration: run a small harness against a pinned model in a CI job with a capped token budget. Module C — Prompt Evals in CI (quality gates) - Objective: fail CI on quality regressions before deployment. - Pattern: create a small eval set (10–50 prompts) with expected outputs or metrics (ROUGE, exact-match, or heuristics). - Example pipeline step: run `python ci/prompt_eval.py --model pinned-v1 --threshold 0.82` and exit non-zero on fail. - Quick tip: keep evals lightweight (static seeds, deterministic sampling) to avoid flakiness. Module D — Canary + Telemetry + Rollback - Objective: deploy changes safely and observe production signals. - Canary strategy: 5% traffic -> 25% -> 100% based on canary checks. - Canary checks (examples): 99th percentile latency < 500ms, error rate < 0.5%, prompt-eval score delta < -0.03 vs baseline. - Rollback: automated if any check trips; notify SRE + owning engineer, revert to pinned model/version. Telemetry contract (minimal event set you should emit): - sdk.call.start: tags=[route, model, request_id, user_tier] - sdk.call.end: fields=[latency_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out, status_code] - sdk.response.quality: fields=[eval_score, eval_id, sample_id] - sdk.error: fields=[error_type, error_message, stack, code] - Implementation guidance: emit as structured JSON to our ingestion endpoint; ensure request_id correlation between all events. Sample CI YAML (conceptual, keep small): - name: Run unit tests run: pytest -q - name: Prompt evals run: python ci/prompt_eval.py --model ${PINNED_MODEL} --threshold 0.82 - name: Canary deploy (scripted) run: ./ci/canary_deploy.sh --model ${CANARY_MODEL} --traffic 5 env: REDWOOD_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.REDWOOD_API_KEY }} ci/prompt_eval.py (sketch): - loads eval corpus (jsonl), runs deterministic generation, computes metric (simple F1 or application-specific rule), prints summary and exits 0/1 depending on threshold. Failure modes and mitigations (practical list): - Flaky evals: reduce randomness, pin seeds, increase sample size. - Token budget blowouts in CI: set strict generation caps, run a short smoke eval in PRs and a longer nightly eval. - Latency spikes in canary: reduce canary traffic, toggle to lower-cost model or cached responses for hot prefixes. - Uncaught hallucination regressions: add targeted golden prompts to eval set and create automatic alerts if they regress. Quick troubleshooting checklist for on-call/dev: (do this in order) 1) Check telemetry: sdk.call.end error rates and latency percentiles. 2) Verify model pin/version used in the environment. 3) Run local prompt_eval.py against the pinned model to reproduce. 4) If canary failing: scale down traffic, revert to previous pinned model, open postmortem ticket. Small sample code snippets (JS + Python variants): - Python local ephemeral client: from redwood import RedwoodClient client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY']) resp = client.generate(model="small-chat-1", prompt=my_prompt, max_tokens=128) - Node (serverless handler): import { Redwood } from 'redwood-sdk' const r = new Redwood(process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY) export default async function handler(req, res) { const out = await r.generate({ model: 'pinned-1', prompt: req.body.prompt }) res.json(out) } Playground exercises (deliverables for each learner): - A branch with: (1) a working sample app, (2) unit tests that mock the model, (3) a CI job that runs evals, (4) a scripted canary deploy command. Checklist before graduation from tutorial: - [ ] Prompt evals added to repo (10–50 samples) - [ ] CI fails on eval regressions - [ ] Telemetry instrumented and visible in dev dashboard - [ ] Canary script exists and documented - [ ] Rollback procedure documented in README Open TODOs for this doc (next steps to make it production-ready): - Convert code snippets into runnable samples in sdk-samples repo (assign PR to Miguel). - Add a lightweight eval dataset template and annotate 20 starter prompts (Samir). - Work with Observability to add a canned dashboard with the telemetry contract fields (Riley). - Draft a short customer-facing one-pager on "How we safely ship prompt changes". Notes to self / quick ideas: keep this workshop terse (2–3 hours max) and highly prescriptive. Avoid long deep dives into Transformer internals — engineers care about repeatability and SLOs. Consider making a 1-hour "fast lane" that covers only the happy path (local -> CI smoke -> canary). References and quick links: - internal sdk-samples repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-samples - CI eval runner proto: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ci-scripts/blob/main/prompt_eval.py - Related docs: CONFLUENCE-3456 (Prompt eval principles) End of draft.
